questions.prompt: Devi has active sessions in Okta, Atlas and Ledger. What should an engineer assume about their state?

options.text: They are separate sessions whose creation, expiry and termination must be considered individually
options.explanation: Federation connects sign-in events without making all applications share one session record.

options.text: They have the same expiry whenever one assertion starts them
options.explanation: Each system has its own session state and policy, subject to applicable federation constraints.

options.text: Closing Atlas necessarily deletes the Okta session
options.explanation: Application navigation does not guarantee provider logout.

options.text: The shortest assertion validity always deletes every session
options.explanation: Assertion acceptance and derived session handling have different rules.

questions.prompt: Devi logs out of Atlas, which terminates only its local session. Her Okta session remains acceptable. What can happen when she immediately opens Atlas again?

options.text: A new SAML exchange can sign her back in without a credential prompt
options.explanation: Local logout ended Atlas's session, but the provider may still authenticate through its own session.

options.text: The old Atlas session must still exist
options.explanation: A newly created session can explain rapid return without the old one surviving.

options.text: Okta must ask for a password every time
options.explanation: An acceptable provider session can avoid a new prompt.

options.text: Ledger must automatically log out
options.explanation: Local Atlas logout does not imply Ledger termination.

questions.prompt: Atlas accepted an assertion at 10:01 whose acceptance deadline was 10:05. Its local session policy permits continued access, subject to applicable authentication-session bounds. What does passing 10:05 mean?

options.text: The assertion can no longer be newly accepted under that deadline; it does not alone define every local session expiry
options.explanation: The message acceptance window is distinct from the lifetime of an already established session.

options.text: Every local session must always end exactly at 10:05
options.explanation: That assumes the assertion acceptance deadline is universally the session deadline.

options.text: The assertion may be replayed forever because a session exists
options.explanation: Existing sessions do not remove assertion acceptance limits.

options.text: The browser must resend the assertion for every page
options.explanation: The local session ordinarily supports subsequent requests.

questions.prompt: Atlas has a 15-minute idle timeout and an 8-hour maximum session lifetime. Devi remains continuously active. Which limit can still end the session?

options.text: The maximum lifetime
options.explanation: Activity can refresh idle state according to policy but does not necessarily extend an absolute maximum.

options.text: Neither limit can ever apply to an active user
options.explanation: Maximum lifetime can apply even with activity.

options.text: The current page activity necessarily refreshes the absolute maximum
options.explanation: An idle refresh does not inherently extend an absolute maximum session lifetime.

options.text: The Okta idle timeout automatically replaces both Atlas limits
options.explanation: Provider and application session policies are separate and must be examined at their respective boundaries.

questions.prompt: A browser still holds an Atlas session cookie after Atlas invalidates the corresponding server-side session. Does the cookie alone guarantee access?

options.text: No; Atlas must recognize an active, acceptable session behind it
options.explanation: A cookie value does not override the server's session validity decision.

options.text: Yes; cookie possession always overrides logout
options.explanation: The server can revoke or expire the referenced session.

options.text: Yes; the cookie becomes a fresh SAML assertion
options.explanation: A local cookie is not an IdP assertion.

options.text: Yes, if the original assertion was signed
options.explanation: A previously accepted signature does not keep a revoked local session active.

questions.prompt: An Okta global session policy allows the existing Okta session, but an application's authentication policy requires additional assurance. What can follow?

options.text: The app's policy can require additional authentication before access
options.explanation: Global session acceptability does not guarantee every application's requirements are already met.

options.text: The app policy is ignored whenever any Okta cookie exists
options.explanation: A provider session does not override all application policy conditions.

options.text: The SP's account database is automatically deleted
options.explanation: Policy evaluation does not have that effect.

options.text: The assertion must be encrypted twice
options.explanation: Policy assurance and XML encryption are separate concerns.

questions.prompt: Atlas requests fresh authentication and receives an acceptable new result. Does that alone guarantee every Atlas session on every device has ended?

options.text: No; session revocation is a separate scope and operation
options.explanation: Fresh authentication for a transaction does not inherently terminate all other local sessions.

options.text: Yes; ForceAuthn means global session deletion
options.explanation: That is not the meaning of the request flag.

options.text: Yes; the request removes every browser cookie
options.explanation: A SAML request does not have universal cookie access.

options.text: Only if the NameID is an email address
options.explanation: Identifier format does not determine revocation scope.

questions.prompt: An SP is configured for Okta-supported basic SP-initiated SAML logout, including the required request signing. What is the essential next step after local initiation?

options.text: Send the correctly signed LogoutRequest to the configured Okta SLO endpoint using the supported binding
options.explanation: SLO is a configured protocol exchange, not merely a local cookie deletion.

options.text: Send the provider's signing private key to the browser
options.explanation: Private-key disclosure is not logout.

options.text: Assume the ACS URL is always also the SLO endpoint
options.explanation: Sign-in and logout endpoints have distinct roles.

options.text: Send a LogoutRequest to any endpoint listed in metadata
options.explanation: The request must use the configured SLO service and supported binding, not an arbitrary metadata endpoint.

questions.prompt: Okta requires signed SP-initiated LogoutRequests. Which public material does Okta need to validate them?

options.text: The configured public certificate corresponding to the SP's logout-request signing key
options.explanation: For this direction, the SP signs and Okta verifies. This differs from verifying Okta-issued sign-in responses.

options.text: Only Okta's own assertion-signing certificate
options.explanation: That verifies signatures made with Okta's key, not the SP's key.

options.text: Only Atlas's encryption public key, regardless of key purpose
options.explanation: A recipient encryption key is not automatically the trusted public key for verifying SP-signed logout requests.

options.text: Any certificate embedded by an unknown browser
options.explanation: Message-supplied certificates do not establish trust by themselves.

questions.prompt: A team assumes Okta's basic SP-initiated SAML SLO response will return by Redirect because its LogoutRequest used Redirect. What should be corrected?

options.text: Check Okta's documented response behavior; basic SAML SLO uses an HTTP-POST return
options.explanation: Request and response bindings need not be symmetric, and product documentation matters.

options.text: Every SAML reply must use the same binding as its request
options.explanation: Bindings can differ across protocol legs.

options.text: SLO responses never travel through a browser
options.explanation: Browser-mediated logout responses are supported.

options.text: The SP should accept only an empty browser response
options.explanation: The documented SLO return is a protocol response that must be handled under its configured agreement.

questions.prompt: A LogoutRequest identifies an authentication session using SessionIndex. What is that value?

options.text: A SAML authentication-session identifier used according to the logout agreement
options.explanation: It helps identify the relevant federated session; it is not automatically the browser's cookie value.

options.text: Always the raw Atlas session cookie
options.explanation: Protocol session identifiers and cookie implementations are distinct.

options.text: The Assertion ID reused as the browser cookie in every product
options.explanation: SessionIndex identifies an authentication session; it is not universally identical to an assertion ID or local cookie.

options.text: The ACS network port
options.explanation: It is not endpoint port configuration.

questions.prompt: A SAML LogoutResponse reports an outer Success with nested PartialLogout. What should the application report?

options.text: A partial logout outcome rather than claiming every participant ended its session
options.explanation: The nested status qualifies the overall result and must be interpreted.

options.text: A guarantee of universal logout
options.explanation: PartialLogout explicitly signals incomplete logout scope.

options.text: An automatic signature failure
options.explanation: Status meaning and signature validity are different checks.

options.text: An instruction to retry every participant indefinitely
options.explanation: PartialLogout reports an incomplete outcome; retries require a controlled implementation policy rather than an indefinite loop.

questions.prompt: A logout participant times out without confirming completion. What should the UI or evidence report say?

options.text: Its session termination is unconfirmed
options.explanation: A timeout is not positive evidence that the participant ended its session.

options.text: Every application is definitely signed out
options.explanation: That overstates the available evidence.

options.text: The user definitely never had a session there
options.explanation: Timeout says nothing conclusive about earlier state.

options.text: The IdP's signing key has necessarily expired
options.explanation: Many failures can cause timeouts; key expiry is not established.

questions.prompt: An organization wants Okta's additional front-channel SLO capability involving participating apps. What must be established first?

options.text: Current feature availability, org enablement, participating-app support and configuration
options.explanation: The feature is conditional, including its documented Early Access status, and should not be assumed from basic SAML support alone.

options.text: Every SAML app participates automatically
options.explanation: Product capability and app participation must be configured and supported.

options.text: Any iframe can delete any site's session cookie
options.explanation: Browser isolation and each participant's behavior still apply.

options.text: Only enable basic local logout in the initiating SP
options.explanation: Local logout does not configure the additional multi-participant front-channel capability.

questions.prompt: A front-channel logout design depends on browser-mediated calls to several apps. Why test it in real supported browsers?

options.text: Browser cookie and embedding behavior can affect whether participants receive and complete the logout steps
options.explanation: The planned protocol flow still depends on actual browser behavior.

options.text: Browsers automatically confirm every server-side session ended
options.explanation: They cannot guarantee a participant's server-side outcome.

options.text: XML signatures disable all browser restrictions
options.explanation: Signatures do not change browser security policy.

options.text: Testing only the IdP's settings proves every app completed logout
options.explanation: Configuration is not end-to-end completion evidence.

questions.prompt: A diagram shows generic SAML back-channel logout using SOAP. What must an engineer avoid claiming without product-specific evidence?

options.text: That every Okta SAML integration supports that SOAP logout path
options.explanation: A standard-level flow is not proof that a particular product or app exposes it.

options.text: That the flow has server-to-server messages
options.explanation: That is the point of a back-channel exchange.

options.text: That participants still need trust checks
options.explanation: Trust requirements remain relevant.

options.text: That delivery and completion can differ
options.explanation: That distinction remains useful in any logout design.

questions.prompt: After local logout, the packet records a new exchange and a different Atlas session. What is justified?

options.text: Later access used replacement state rather than proving the old session survived
options.explanation: Independent provider state can support a new SSO transaction after local logout.

options.text: The old Atlas session necessarily survived
options.explanation: The packet records its invalidation and a distinct new session.

options.text: Local logout automatically ended every Ledger session
options.explanation: No Ledger termination is supplied.

options.text: The assertion must have been replayed
options.explanation: The packet states that the new exchange used fresh messages.

evidence: New sign-in: fresh request/response; acceptable Okta session reused
New Atlas session S2: created; projects allowed
questions.reasoning: Before choosing, explain which observation supports your conclusion and which outcome this packet does not establish.

questions.prompt: Atlas confirms local termination and Ledger times out without a confirmed result. What remains unknown?

options.text: Whether Ledger actually ended the targeted session
options.explanation: An absent completion response establishes uncertainty, not positive evidence either way.

options.text: Whether Atlas's local termination was confirmed
options.explanation: That confirmation is supplied directly.

options.text: Whether the request to Ledger timed out
options.explanation: The timeout itself is an observed fact; the missing result leaves the participant session outcome unconfirmed.

options.text: Whether a timeout proves Ledger kept the session
options.explanation: It does not; processing might occur even when a result is lost.

evidence: Ledger completion or subsequent session evidence: not supplied
questions.reasoning: Before choosing, explain which observation supports your conclusion and which outcome this packet does not establish.

questions.prompt: Assignment removal blocks new federation access, but no app-session revocation is configured. What is the key distinction?

options.text: Future sign-in eligibility does not establish immediate termination of an existing app session
options.explanation: Check the application's actual session and supported revocation behavior.

options.text: Every existing app session necessarily ended at assignment removal
options.explanation: The packet supplies no mechanism or evidence for that claim.

options.text: Every existing app session necessarily lasts forever
options.explanation: Absence of immediate revocation does not remove other session expiry policies.

options.text: The user's NameID must change immediately
options.explanation: Assignment and identifier value are separate concerns.

evidence: Okta assignment: removed; new app sign-in: blocked
Existing Atlas session: present before removal
Immediate downstream revocation mechanism: not configured

questions.prompt: Okta brokers an upstream IdP to Atlas. Atlas and Okta end their sessions, but the upstream IdP session remains. What can happen?

options.text: A later sign-in may reuse the upstream session if policy allows
options.explanation: Logout scope must be traced through each participating relationship; upstream state is independent.

options.text: The upstream session must have been deleted automatically
options.explanation: Downstream logout does not prove upstream termination.

options.text: Atlas must still have its old local session
options.explanation: A new federation journey can explain the return.

options.text: The upstream provider can never issue another assertion
options.explanation: Its remaining session may support subsequent issuance.
